# Reasons for purchase

## Purchase drivers depth analysis

### Functional drivers

#### Driver I: Turn data into end-to-end business stream

|  |
| --- |
| Clients are usually not “no software”, but rather too many software, forms and chat tools. The real purchase objective is to reduce duplicate entries and allow sales, procurement, warehousing, finance and management to work around the same data. |
| Corresponding product values: harmonized data model, cross-module trigger, API/database connection, business questions. |

#### Driver II: Rapid adaptation to non-standardized processes

|  |
| --- |
| The systems and operations of growing enterprises are still changing, and the traditional ERP two is slow and expensive, and the purely standard cloud service is not very relevant. Visualization brings not “development for all” as a core value, but rather a change in business that does not wait in line for IT. |
| Corresponding product values: forms, processes, reports, portals, templates and custom operations. |

#### Driver III: Let AI move from "response to questions" to "implementation"

|  |
| --- |
| Businesses ' new sense of universal chat robots has declined and are more willing to pay for automatic filing, filling, generating quotations, triggering approvals, forecasting inventories and synchronizing assignments. |
| Corresponding product value: Job intelligence, AI CRM, procurement request price, meeting to-do, cross-system implementation. |

#### Driver IV: Security and control

|  |
| --- |
| Conference, client, contractual, financial and personnel data are sensitive. Privatization deployments, competencies, logs and enterprise-owned servers will significantly increase the willingness to monitor clients ' payments. |
| Corresponding product values: privatization, enterprise-level security, data segregation, logs, letter creation and certification. |

#### Driver V: Cross-regional collaboration with weak networks

|  |
| --- |
| For cross-border trade, overseas branches, factories and remote service teams, multilingual, real-time captioning, standardized documentation and low-bandwidth meetings are business continuity requirements rather than mere optimization. |

### Economic drivers

|  |
| --- |
| Reducing the cost of multiple software subscriptions and interface maintenance; |
| (b) Reduction in the capacity of reporting, recording, checking, summary and reminder staff; |
| Reducing stock backlogs, stock shortages, procurement price differentials and payment errors; |
| Shortening the sales, approval, delivery and recovery cycles; |
| One-time customized development with subscription and visual configuration alternatives; |
| Reducing the cost of digital failure through sector pilots. |
| The really valid ROI formula should read: |
| ** Annualization gain = time cost saving + error/loss reduction + turnover and conversion improvement - software subscription - implementation and integration - training and migration - ongoing ** |

### Emotional and identity dynamics

|  |
| --- |
| Enterprise software purchases are not entirely rational and include the following: |
| The boss wants to move from “person-to-person” to “data pipe”; |
| The manager wishes to demonstrate, at the request of the board or consortium, that AI has produced operational results; |
| IT wants to move away from endless and sporadic development needs; |
| Chiefs of operations want to reduce cross-sectoral privation and increase controllability; |
| The employee wants to get rid of repeated work but fears being monitored or replaced by AI. |
| The acceptance of AI by relevant actors is often influenced by both a “advanced sense” and a “safe sense of security” and by concerns about controllability, auditability and traceability. |

### Social and policy drivers

|  |
| --- |
| Sectors such as the Ministry of Industry and Communications have promoted the digital transformation of SMEs, explicitly requiring the provision of “small and light” solutions around “resistance to turn, afraid to turn, unable to turn”, with emphasis on downside, efficiency gains, safety and industry suitability. |
| [Source: Ministry of Industry and Communications, 2025 Pilot Notification] (https://www.miit.gov.cn/xwfb/gxdt/sjdt/art/2025/art_2764fad98e3f45b5af7e1258a8cdbf8d.html) |
| Policies provide a market environment for low-cost, rapid deployment and industry-appropriate digital products. The actual purchasing judgement of the enterprise remains linked to business effectiveness, conditions of implementation and service capacity. |
